title: Production Planning Software: When Does a Manufacturer Actually Need It?
description:
Many factories run on a planner who stitches together ERP dates, spreadsheets, whiteboards and phone calls until the plan breaks. This episode helps manufacturing and operations leaders recognize the warning signs that manual planning has hit its limit and shows how to introduce planning software that produces feasible, explainable schedules.
In this episode
00:00 – The planner as the planning system01:40 – What production planning means06:20 – When spreadsheets and experience still work11:07 – Six warning signs40:31 – Where ERP and MES reach their limits50:28 – What planning software does and the data model65:04 – Fix the process, start with one decision96:09 – Fabric, Power BI and Power Platform
Key takeaways
Production planning software becomes necessary when changes, shared resources and dependencies outpace what planners can test manually, not when the company reaches a certain size.ERP owns demand and materials and MES records execution, while a planning layer must test feasible sequences against real capacity, setup, material and qualification constraints.Start with one failing decision, a clear process and trusted product, process and resource data, run the new plan in parallel, and use Fabric, Power BI and Power Platform around the engine, not instead of it.
Worth quoting
“The word feasible matters more than fast. A schedule can look neat and still fail the moment production tries to follow it.” – Mirko Peters (03:38)
“The issue isn't whether people use Excel. It's whether Excel and experience can still keep pace with change.” – Mirko Peters (10:50)
